Title: Tzimisce gr2-3 wall : Burn after reading

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Deck Name : Burn after reading
Author : Ankha
Description :

How do you intend to oust?
Mainly by protecting the Smiling Jack and/or Constant Revolution to the death. Occasionally bleeding for 1.
The goal is not only to catch the minions coming by, but also to burn them using aggravated damage.

How do you intend to keep from being ousted?
Deflecting the bleed and blocking+burning the minions.

What do you want your ready region to look like (ie, how many guys are you planning on getting out)?
3 vampires, with an additional Ghoul, a Corpse Balloon, and maybe an Abbot.

What do you want your average turn to look like?
Staying untapped to protect the Smiling Jack, but occasionally equipping or recruiting.

What problems have you observed with the deck in play?
I haven't played it yet, but i'm not sure at all of the wakes/intercept/combat proportions. Need help there

I guess I could put a Milicent Smith or two in the deck, as well as a Scourge of the Enochians and a Fear of Mekhet ("burn! burn! burn!") Rötschreck and DI would fit in too.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
Why telepathic tracking instead of Rotschrek ? Both serve the same purpose and Rotschrek tend to have the job better done. Because of too many master already ?

Are you sure for the Path of Metamorphosis with only 9 card to gain from ? While you can defend it, you won't do too much with it.

If the goal is to do aggravated damage, why so "few" breath of dragon and so many Horrid Form ?

Given the indiscriminate nature of the damage dealing card, shouldn't Telepathic Misdirection be a lot better than My ennemy's ennemy ?

With this list, I would fear to kill everyone on the table except my prey, since it will be the least pressured player of the table. I would somehow try to find space for Fiendish Tongue and Changelin to put a little pressure on my prey.

I may suggest then to look at Body Arsenal, especially if you keep Path of Meta and Inner Essence. With a blood cost reduction (either the path, inner Essence, or some vampires) you can play it for the same price as a Chiroptean, and the cumulable +1 strength make you more likely to burn a vampire.

It's still a card a tad too costly for its effect. But if you want to burn people, it may be worth considering. Maybe 2-3 so that people fear burning even at 3 blood ?

> Ankha wrote:
> It's always a risk with Smiling Jack. That's where skill may be needed so everything works fine.
>
I understand skill help, but if your prey bloat more than anyone else I don't exactly see how you will kill it, especially since you can't pressure it specifically. An unnamed / enkil cog setting for example seem pretty unbeatable without heavy table help.

Messages.Author: Lemminkäinen
Messages.Body: Anarch Revolts and Armies of Rats could put pressure on your prey specifically (well, AR does so as long as you let others go Anarch). Army of Rats seems like an especially good fit since there's already so many things craving (D)action removal or stealing in your deck.

Messages.Body:

> With this list, I would fear to kill everyone on the table except my prey, since it will be the least pressured player of the table. I would somehow try to find space for Fiendish Tongue and Changelin to put a little pressure on my prey.

IMO that's a good point and a workaround to keep the prey from running away would be to use more Eagle's Sight. I'd suggest at between 5-7 depending on deckspace.

In addition I'd focus more on Lambach. Regarding the burning of vampires he's very card efficient with his build in +1 strength and special.
